brief: Goldman expects US corporate equity issuance to total $600bn in 2027, up from a 2026 pace ($431bn YTD, +98% y/y, on track to surpass 2021's $540bn record) that slowed sharply in Q3 ($93bn, down from Q2's record $252bn) as sharp rate rises (10-year yields up ~125bp over the year, a 2-standard-deviation move) and narrowing S&P 500 breadth (median stock 16% below its high) weighed on IPO conditions. The 2027 forecast ($175bn IPOs, $425bn other primary, 0.8% of market cap) rests on solid growth, rising equity prices, declining rates (GS sees 10-year yields falling to 4.4% by year-end 2027) and AI investment. AI-related follow-ons are 45% of 2026 follow-on volume ($65bn), dwarfed by roughly $600bn of AI-related debt issuance; GS expects hyperscaler cash flow and debt together to exceed capex in 2027-28, limiting their own equity need, though some issued anyway in 2026. Demand should offset supply: buybacks are forecast at $1.7tn in 2027 (from $1.5tn), aided by NVDA's $235bn authorization, plus growing cash M&A and over $1tn of household/foreign buying in H1 2026. Including expiring lockups, net supply should still rise by the most since 2000, pressuring valuations without derailing the bull market, GS argues, partly because light investor positioning leaves little need to sell into new issuance.
